subject: Q2 Customer Health: SignalBox renewal risk register & exec attention
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q2 Customer Health: SignalBox renewal risk register & exec attention

Team —

We need to consolidate a short renewal-risk register for SignalBox ahead of Monday's QBR prep meeting (QBR materials due EOD Monday). This account is showing mixed signals and should be on the exec radar. High-level context: BrightCore (SignalBox product) runs a high-volume serving workload, has committed reserved capacity, and is asking about a potential SLA exception + 10% price ask in their draft renewal.

Quick status (from last week):
- Usage: steady at 88% committed capacity, spikes weekly during batch runs.
- Recent incident: 2028-05-24 degraded throughput for 90m (root cause a bad kernel fallback).
- CS score: 6.8/10 (their CSM flagged slower model upgrades & higher token costs).

Requesting the following by EOD Monday:
1) One-paragraph health summary we can put on the first slide (owner: Lauren).
2) Two top renewal risks with mitigation and owner tag (owner: Jordan for contract/legal / procurement asks; Priyom for technical mitigations).
3) Any outstanding procurement/legal blockers + proposed ask to execs (if we need approval for credit, pricing flexibility, or SLA exceptions).
4) Attach latest health snapshot and a short note on whether we recommend a canary rollout or force immediate patch.

Attendees for Monday's prep: me, Lauren, Jordan, Priyom, and I will invite Maria from BrightCore if we decide to surface the pricing ask.

I put a stub slide in the Drive (link below) — keep bullet items crisp.

Thanks — Markus

--
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 Customer Health: SignalBox renewal risk register & exec attention

Markus —

Health one-liner for slide (draft): 
SignalBox shows stable throughput with episodic latency spikes tied to weekly batch runs; recent regression reduced margin on committed capacity — recommend targeted quantization + two-week canary for patch.

Top risks (short):
1) Cost erosion risk — Token/unit costs trending +8% vs committed baseline; customer cites higher tail-latency inefficiency. Mitigation: propose tailored quantization profile + auto-batching policy change; owner: Priyom; ETA: 2 weeks for canary.
2) Contractual ask — BrightCore is requesting a 10% price concession and an SLA exception for monthly uptime during batch windows. Mitigation: We can offer a one-time credit (4 weeks) conditioned on a 6-month committed extension, or provide an operational playbook and runbook to limit batch impact; owner: Jordan; ask to exec: approve up to 8% concession or sign-off on alternate SLA language.

Attachments: I attached a compact health snapshot and the performance traces for the incident (SignalBox_health_snapshot_20280601.pdf).

Notes on the incident: root cause was our kernel fallback under an unexpected sequence length distribution; a code patch is ready but needs canary testing. Priyom, recommend we list the canary test matrix in the prep meeting.

— Lauren
Product Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

Adding contract/legal perspective: 

- Procurement has pushed a draft that requests a pricing floor and an SLA exception window (0200–0500 PT) for the nightly batch loads. They are also asking for a 12-month rate lock.
- Our leverage: account has been with us 18 months; committed capacity = material to our dedicated pool. We should aim to preserve margin while minimizing executive concessions.

Recommended exec asks for Monday (short bullets):
A) Approve one-time operational credit up to $75k in exchange for a 6–12 month extension;
B) Approve an SLA addendum limited to batch windows with explicit bounded credits and telemetry gating;
C) Approve a short-term price flexibility corridor up to 8% (if we cannot meet B).

If we want to push back harder, procurement will push a competitive procurement loop — they mentioned evaluating alternate vendors for latency-critical endpoints. That would increase churn risk.

I can draft suggested language for the SLA addendum and a short memo on revenue impact. Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Markus / team —

Thanks for the transparency. A few clarifications from BrightCore: 
- The 10% pricing ask is a request from finance to offset token-cost growth; they will consider a blended approach (credit + term extension).
- The SLA exception is specifically requested for the nightly batch window (0200–0500 PT) where our legacy batch jobs briefly spike concurrency. We are open to telemetry gating and reduced credit exposure if Redwood can present a mitigation plan that keeps our production SLAs intact.
- Timing: BrightCore procurement needs a proposed commercial framework by end of week to present to their procurement committee next Tuesday.

Can you include a simple pricing scenario table and the operational runbook you propose? We'll review and aim to align before procurement meeting.

Regards,
Maria Gonzalez
Director, Cloud Ops — BrightCore

Thanks everyone — consolidated ask below for the exec slide and the QBR packet. I copied Maria so BrightCore procurement sees the timeline.

Executive summary (single line): SignalBox shows steady consumption but is at risk of margin erosion from elevated token costs and a requested 10% pricing concession; recommend conditional credit + operational canary to preserve margin and customer relationship.

Renewal risk register (short):
- Risk 1: Price concession request (10%) — Impact: ARR erosion if granted; Probability: medium-high; Mitigation: Offer 4 weeks credit + 6–12 month term extension; Exec ask: Approve credit up to $75k OR price flexibility up to 8%. Owner: Jordan.
- Risk 2: Performance regression during batch windows — Impact: customer SLA concerns and procurement leverage; Probability: medium; Mitigation: Rapid canary (2 weeks) of quantization patch + auto-batching; Exec ask: Approve prioritized rollout and dedicated engineering bandwidth for canary. Owner: Priyom.
- Risk 3: Procurement timeline mismatch — Impact: compresses negotiation window; Probability: high (proc expects a framework by next Tue); Mitigation: Deliver pricing scenarios + short runbook by EOW; Owner: Lauren.

Attachments for QBR packet: SignalBox_health_snapshot_20280601.pdf, SLA_exception_request.docx, SignalBox_MA_Pricing_Summary.xlsx

Immediate asks to execs (for slide):
1) Approve a one-time credit up to $75k OR pre-approve up to 8% price corridor.
2) Approve dedicated engineering hours (2 FTE-weeks) for canary rollout and monitoring.
3) Sign-off on conditional SLA addendum language (Jordan to provide language).

Next steps: Lauren to finalize slide text & health snapshot; Jordan to draft SLA addendum and pricing scenarios; Priyom to publish canary test plan (matrix + monitoring dashboard). Please mark done in the Drive doc or reply with any redlines by EOD Tuesday so we can finalize the packet.

Markus
